title: Console inline help & focus mapping for metric rollups (a11y + i18n)
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Problem: Metric rollups and compact cost panels present dense numeric data and contextual controls that are currently hard to discover or navigate by keyboard/screen readers and render inconsistently across locales (numbers, units, spacing). Goal: Add inline contextual help (microcopy/tooltips), normalize focus order and skip targets for metric groups, and make metric updates announceable in a non-disruptive way while preserving pluralization and locale-aware numeric formatting.
acceptance_criteria: Keyboard tab order follows a predictable spatial-to-logical mapping for metric cards and rollup controls (Skip-to-metrics at top, then per-card interactive controls)

All inline help text is available as visible microcopy and as accessible tooltips (aria-describedby) with 4.5:1 contrast for body text and 3:1 for tooltips where allowed by WCAG 2.1 AA large text and guidance
Live-updating metric values are announced via aria-live="polite" for non-critical updates; assertive only used for threshold breach events (customer-facing alert), documented in console SLOs
Number formatting respects user locale (grouping separators, decimal, non-breaking space for SI units) and RTL locales mirror layout while preserving focus order
Design tokens updated for contrast delta the console color system to ensure >=4.5:1 for small numeric labels on all themes in colorblind simulations
Prototype tested with NVDA, VoiceOver, and ChromeVox; results documented with at least 3 screen-reader scenarios
Engineering PR with keyboard mapping and aria attributes merged and e2e tests added for focus order and localized formatting
engineering_notes: Preferred implementation: add logical container elements with role=group and aria-labelledby using the card heading ID; avoid tabindex on non-interactives; use CSS order only when accompanied by DOM order changes for screen readers
Expose a console setting 'compact-metrics-announce' (default: polite) to allow customers to opt-in to reduced verbosity for high-throughput dashboards
Add i18n hooks so formatNumber(value, locale, {unit, style, maximumFractionDigits}) is used everywhere metric numbers are rendered
accessibility_notes: WCAG targets: 2.4.3 Focus Order, 1.4.3 Contrast (AA), 4.1.2 Name, Role, Value
Use aria-describedby for contextual microcopy; ensure descriptions are concise (<=140 chars) and not repeated verbatim by screen readers
When collapsing metric groups, set aria-expanded and provide a visible indicator + offscreen text announcing the collapse state for SR users
Use role=status for live region fallback in browsers that don't support aria-live politeness levels reliably
Avoid assertive announcements for routine background updates to prevent screen reader jank; reserve for customer-impact thresholds
localization_notes: Coordinate with i18n team for plural rules (CLDR) for units like 'request', 'reqs', 'requests/sec' using ICU message syntax
Numbers should use thin non-breaking space for thousands in fr-FR and ru-RU where applicable; use locale-sensitive unit spacing
RTL: mirror layout but preserve source order for announcements. Add tests in Arabic (ar-SA) and Hebrew (he-IL) locales
Microcopy translations: provide context notes (max length 100 chars) to translators to avoid truncation in compact cards
review_comments: Priya Singh (PM): 'Agree with polite live region default — we saw support calls when we used assertive in an earlier sprint.'
Marco Alvarez (Engineering): 'Will need a small perf budget to avoid extra DOM nodes; prefer reuse of existing card containers instead of wrapper divs.'
Design Peer (Kaitlyn Zhou): 'Microcopy examples look good; propose a short variant for narrow breakpoints to avoid wrapping.'
Accessibility SME (Nadav Cohen): 'Contrast target must be enforced in tokens, not ad-hoc CSS. Add a token mapping table.'
